value.body: Helps projects and companies assess and report their environmental impact — for example environmental impact assessments (EIA), monitoring reports and documents for environmental clearance. Environmental consultancies, engineering firms and some NGOs hire for this role. Work mixes field surveys, data work and report writing.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc Environmental Science, or a B.Tech
items.note: An M.Sc is common for EIA roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Spreadsheets, GIS, air / water monitoring data, report templates

items.label: Framework
items.value: EIA process under the Environment (Protection) Act

items.label: Postgraduate enrolment, Environmental Science
items.note: Students in PG programmes in the subject, not working consultants
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 13, actual responses

items.label: Ph.D. enrolment, Environmental Science
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 13, actual responses

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join consultancies as trainee or junior consultants, usually helping with baseline surveys, data compilation and report drafting. An M.Sc in Environmental Science and knowledge of the EIA process and pollution norms are what most hiring looks for.

value.title: At a glance
items: Project deadlines and site visits are common.
Growth path: junior consultant → consultant → project manager or functional area expert.
Work volume follows infrastructure and industrial project activity.

value.title: Postgraduate enrolment in Environmental Science
value.note: Based on institutions that responded to AISHE each year, so part of the change can come from reporting coverage.
